title: Three Ways to Talk About the Future

sections.title: Putting them side by side
sections.content: You now have three tools for the future, and each answers a slightly different question. Present tense + a time word states a fixed fact about what's already arranged. fog + infinitive states a prediction, intention, or promise. tervez + infinitive names an active plan you're deciding and working out. The same underlying event can often be described all three ways, depending on which angle you're taking.

sections.title: Same trip, three angles
rows: Jövő héten meglátogatjuk Ildikót és Gábort.
a prediction about how it will go

items.spanish: Jövő héten meglátogatjuk Ildikót és Gábort.
items.english: Next week we're visiting Ildikó and Gábor.
We'll probably talk a lot with Gábor.
We're planning to rest a lot over the weekend.

sections.content: When in doubt, ask yourself: is this already fixed (present tense), a guess or promise about what will happen (fog), or a decision I'm actively making (tervez)? All three can appear in the very same conversation about the very same event.
